description: The closed vocabulary `emit-ui` already renders (crates/compiler/src/ui_gen.rs + ui_gen_template.html; see crates/compiler/UI_DSL_TODO.md's own build tracker). This file documents the existing manifest wire shape as data -- it does not change what ui_gen.rs emits or what typeck/grammar_export consume today (rfcs/0009 Phase 0). Field names below are the actual camelCase JSON keys `ui_gen.rs`'s `*_json` functions emit, not the internal Rust struct field names.

entries.columns: number, required (typeck-enforced), default 1 if absent from JSON

grid.limitation: no per-child column-span control -- each child occupies the next cell, disclosed narrowing not an oversight (ast.rs LayoutNode::Grid doc comment)

field.field: the resolved FieldSpec JSON (see `fieldSpec` below), embedded directly -- not a name the client looks up a second time
field.resolution: by name against the screen's own fields, typechecked (typeck::check_screen_layout)

action.action: the resolved Action JSON (see `action` below), embedded directly
action.resolution: by display label against the screen's declared or inferred actions, typechecked

widget.closedVocabulary: typeck.rs::check_screen_layout rejects any kind not in this list AND not a linked ui_plugin::NativeUiComponent's name (rfcs/0009 Phase B, Checker.extra_widget_kinds) -- still closed either way, just extensible by whoever calls generate_with_ui_components in Rust source, never by a `.nir` program itself

entries.source: identifier, used by `timeline` to name the backing fn
entries.title: string, used by `card`
entries.*: every other key, generically, for a plugin-contributed kind's own render_js to read via node.entries.<key> (ui_gen.rs::widget_entry_json) -- literals/idents only (Str/Int/Float/Bool/Ident), anything else serializes as null

fieldSpec._comment: ui_gen.rs::field_json -- one form field or table column

keys.name: string
keys.label: string -- a readonly field's *type* label (e.g. "box i64"); ignored for editable controls
keys.displayLabel: string|null -- screen { field <name> { label: "..." } } override; null keeps the raw field name
keys.nested: FieldSpec[] -- populated only when control == "struct", one level deep
keys.options: string[] -- populated only when control == "select"/"searchable_select": zero-payload enum variant names, in declaration order (this order is the field's ordinal meaning, e.g. RiskRating{Low,Medium,High})
keys.requiredViewRoles: string[]|null -- any-of role gate; empty/null = ungated
keys.selectTable: string|null -- generic table-route backing a searchable_select
keys.selectFn: string|null -- fn backing a searchable_select instead

controls._comment: ui_gen.rs::build_field -- Ty -> control inference, or an explicit screen{field{control:...}} override. 7 base controls + searchable_select, per crates/compiler/UI_DSL_TODO.md's own count.

date.inferredFrom: Ty::Str, when the field name looks date-like (is_date_like_field_name)

select.inferredFrom: a zero-payload-only enum reference (the categorical/ordinal case)

searchable_select.inferredFrom: never inferred -- only via explicit screen{field{control:"searchable_select"}}, backed by selectTable or selectFn

struct.inferredFrom: a struct-typed field/param, one nesting level deep (build_field's depth cap)

readonly.inferredFrom: anything else: a payload-carrying enum, anything past the nesting cap, or any type with no editable mapping

action._comment: ui_gen.rs::action_json -- one button/call, CRUD-inferred or screen{action{...}}-declared

keys.kind: "list" | "create" | "update" | "delete" | "get" | "custom" | "source" -- "custom" is a declared screen{action{...}}; "source" is a workspace panel's backing fn, reusing this shape purely for its gating fields
keys.badges: string[] -- effect badges (e.g. "network") from effects::infer_effects, display-only, never gates anything
keys.params: FieldSpec[] -- the action's own call parameters, not assumed to match the subject struct's fields
keys.label: string|null -- set only when kind == "custom"; a CRUD action's label is derived client-side from kind
keys.style: "filled" | "outlined" | null -- null falls back to the client's per-kind default
keys.confirm: string|null -- when set, client must confirm before calling fn (delete always does this unconditionally already)
keys.showResult: bool -- only true on a fn returning Result(json, _), typeck-enforced (check_action_show_result)

charts._comment: MetricRender (dashboard tiles/charts) and PanelRender (workspace panels) share this vocabulary. Rendered as inline SVG, zero external charting library -- ui_gen_template.html's own "self-contained, no external deps" stance.

bar_chart.dataShape: [{label, value}] -- e.g. a chart_<name>() fn, or db_query aliasing columns label/value

chart._comment: rfcs/0009 Phase A -- a fifth, parameterized `visual { render: "chart" ... }` kind, additive alongside the four fixed shapes above (which are unaffected -- "chart" is not a replacement or a desugaring target for them). A bounded grammar-of-graphics subset: mark x encoding instead of a fixed shape per chart type.
appliesTo: metric (dashboard `visual` only -- not yet wired into workspace `panel`)

encoding._comment: one or more `encode <channel> { field, type, aggregate? }` blocks, DSL-side folded into visual's flat entries as "encode.<channel>.<key>" (parser.rs::parse_encode_channel_entries); manifest-side reassembled into this array (ui_gen.rs::parse_chart_config/metrics_json).
encoding.field: any string literal -- NOT cross-checked against a real column; the backing fn returns opaque json, there's no struct to resolve it against (a real, disclosed limit, not an oversight)

panelRenders._comment: PanelRender's own default (a plain table) has no MetricRender equivalent -- a dashboard tile is never a table.

themeTokens._comment: ui_gen.rs::Theme and friends -- MD3 tokens threaded from protobox's DesignSpec via --theme. Every field is optional; an absent field keeps the app's built-in default, byte-for-byte, for every app that predates a given token.
themeTokens.neutral: object<string,string>|null -- same 11-step shape, page background/borders/text hierarchy

motion.animations: string[] -- subset of the fixed 4-name vocabulary ["fade-in","slide-up","scale-in","pop"] the client's @keyframes block hardcodes

layout.appShell: "auto" | "sidebar" | "topbar" | "sidebar-topbar" | "minimal" -- "auto"/absent keeps the fixed nav-rail + top-app-bar shell every pre-existing app already has

themeTokens.valueSafety: every CSS value here is rejected outright if it contains any of < > { } -- theme_value_is_safe's own rule, the only thing standing between a theme file and breaking out of a <style> element

extensionPoints._comment: rfcs/0009 Phase A and Phase B's *mechanism* are both built and verified (see charts.chart above and widget.kinds' closedVocabulary note) -- what remains open is named here, not silently dropped.
extensionPoints.charts: [DONE, mechanism] `render: "chart"` (see charts.chart above). [OPEN] the same mark/encoding config isn't wired into workspace `panel { ... }` yet, only dashboard `visual { ... }` -- PanelRender's own closed set is untouched.
extensionPoints.components: [DONE, mechanism] a Rust crate hand-assembles a `ui_plugin::NativeUiComponent` slice and passes it to `typecheck_optional_main_with_ui_components`/`generate_with_ui_components` (crates/compiler/tests/ui_plugin.rs is the real, screenshot-verified proof). [OPEN] Cargo-metadata-tagged automatic discovery (`kind = "nir-ui-component"` in a dependency's own Cargo.toml, `nirdosha build`/`emit-ui` finding+linking it with no hand-assembled Rust slice) is explicitly not built -- shares one open discovery problem with rfcs/0008 Phase 3 (native builtin auto-discovery) rather than inventing a second, parallel mechanism. [OPEN] a component only ever contributes a `layout` widget kind today, not a full catalog-schema entry (typed `props`, a chart/control/action type, a GBNF fragment, crate-name+version provenance in this file) -- rfcs/0009's original, larger sketch for `NativeUiComponent`.
